sources.title: FTC: How to recognize and avoid phishing scams

sections.body: A scam is a trick to get your money, your passwords or your personal information.
Warning signs: 'You WON a prize!', 'Hurry, only 5 minutes left!', 'Click this link to claim', or messages asking for passwords or codes.
Scammers use excitement or fear to make you act fast without thinking.
The rule: STOP, don't click, and show a trusted adult.
Real companies will never ask for your password in a message.
With a grown-up, look at a spam folder together (don't click anything!). Can you spot the warning signs?

quiz.q: A message says: 'You won a free phone! Click now, offer ends in 2 minutes!' What is the biggest warning sign?
hints: Why would someone want you to hurry?
Scammers don't want you to stop and think.
Example: 'Your account will be closed in 1 hour unless you log in here!' uses the same trick. What trick is it?
quiz.explain: Rushing you is a classic scam trick, so you act before you think or ask someone.

quiz.q: A game chat says a moderator needs your password to give you free coins. You should…
options: Never share it and tell an adult
hints: Would a real company need your password?
Example: a real bank never asks for your PIN by message. Games are the same.
quiz.explain: Real moderators never need your password. Keep it secret and tell an adult.

hints: Strong passwords are long and hard to guess.
Which one would a stranger never guess?
Example: 'sunshine' is weak, but 'Blue7!Rocket?Tree' is strong. Why?
quiz.explain: Long, random words with symbols and numbers are much harder to guess.
